requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects for IPv4 networking on node1.
requirements.summary: The live accept_redirects values were zero for all, default, eth0, and lo before reboot. After a confirmed reboot, the persistent configuration remained present, the sysctl boot service was running, and every observed IPv4 scope again had accept_redirects=0.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets for IPv4 networking on node1.
requirements.summary: The live accept_source_route values were zero for all, default, eth0, and lo before reboot. After a confirmed reboot, the persistent configuration remained present, the sysctl boot service was running, and every observed IPv4 scope again had accept_source_route=0.

overall_summary: Both requested IPv4 hardening outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre- and post-reboot observations demonstrate persistent configuration and active zero values across all detected interface scopes. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: it includes a healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement and observed disconnect, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered sysctl and network state.
limitations: No packet-injection test exercised an actual ICMP redirect or source-routed packet; verification relies on the authoritative live kernel controls.
The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported on Alpine, although the relevant OpenRC sysctl service was directly shown healthy before and after reboot.
A reboot helper log remained in /tmp, and its redacted contents were not available for inspection.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related mutations were appropriately bounded: the executor created and corrected the sysctl policy, applied it, restarted the sysctl service, and rebooted for the mandatory persistence protocol. The only unnecessary mutation was the reboot helper log created under /tmp by cmd-c4d67c21d68447c4; it remained after execution rather than being cleaned up. No new listeners or package damage attributable to the executor were observed.
